summary: Du'a (supplication) is the most direct act of worship — the servant calling upon their Lord. The Prophet (peace be upon him) called it 'the essence of worship' and taught precise etiquettes and times of acceptance to maximise its effectiveness.
content:
Du'a (supplication) is among the most beloved acts of worship in Islam. The Prophet (peace be upon him) declared: 'Du'a is worship' (Abu Dawud 1479 — sahih), and in another narration: 'Du'a is the brain (marrow) of worship' (Tirmidhi 3371 — hasan). Allah commands it directly and promises response: 'And your Lord says: Call upon Me; I will respond to you' (40:60).

Unlike formal ritual prayers (salah), du'a has no fixed time, form, or language requirement — it is the heart's direct address to Allah, available at every moment, in every condition, in any language.

## The Etiquettes of Du'a

Classical scholars identified etiquettes (adab) that make du'a more likely to be accepted:

**1. Beginning with praise and salawat:** Start by praising Allah (al-hamd) and sending blessings upon the Prophet (salawat). The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Every du'a is veiled until the person sends blessings upon the Prophet' (Abu Dawud 1481 — hasan).

**2. Raising the hands:** The Prophet (peace be upon him) raised his hands when making du'a (Bukhari 1031 in the context of istisqa; Muslim 895). Imam al-Nawawi noted this is among the most recommended acts during du'a.

**3. Facing the qiblah:** Recommended in congregational du'a contexts (as in istisqa).

**4. Certainty and sincerity:** Make du'a with certainty that Allah can and will answer: 'When one of you makes du'a, let him be resolute in asking and not say: O Allah, if You will, give me — for there is none who can compel Allah' (Bukhari 6339, Muslim 2679).

**5. Calling upon Allah by His names:** 'And to Allah belong the best names, so invoke Him by them' (7:180). Begin du'a with the name most relevant to the need — 'Ya Rahman, Ya Rahim' for mercy; 'Ya Ghaffar' for forgiveness; 'Ya Razzaq' for provision.

**6. Avoiding haram:** The Prophet (peace be upon him) described a man who raises his hands crying 'Ya Rabb, Ya Rabb' — yet his food is haram, his drink is haram, his clothing is haram, and he was nourished on the haram. 'How could he be answered?' (Muslim 1015). Avoiding the prohibited is a condition for du'a to be accepted.

**7. Persisting without haste:** 'The du'a of any one of you is answered as long as he is not hasty and says: I made du'a but it was not answered' (Bukhari 6340, Muslim 2735).

## Times When Du'a Is More Likely Accepted

The Sunnah identifies times of special acceptance:

**The last third of the night:** Allah descends (in a manner befitting His majesty) and calls: 'Who is supplicating Me that I may respond? Who is asking Me that I may give? Who is seeking My forgiveness that I may forgive?' (Bukhari 1145, Muslim 758).

**Between the adhan and iqamah:** 'Du'a between the adhan and the iqamah is not rejected' (Tirmidhi 212 — sahih).

**In prostration (sujud):** 'The servant is closest to his Lord when prostrating, so increase du'a there' (Muslim 482).

**The day of Arafah:** The best du'a is the du'a of the Day of Arafah (Tirmidhi 3585 — hasan).

**The last hour of Friday:** A special hour on Friday when du'a is accepted (Bukhari 935, Muslim 852).

**When fasting, at the time of breaking fast:** 'Three whose du'a is not rejected: the fasting person when breaking fast, the just ruler, and the oppressed person' (Tirmidhi 3598 — hasan).

## Selected Du'as from the Sunnah

**For forgiveness:**
Sayyid al-Istighfar: 'Allahumma anta Rabbi, la ilaha illa anta, khalaqtani wa ana 'abduk, wa ana 'ala 'ahdika wa wa'dika mas-tata't, a'udhu bika min sharri ma sana't, abu'u laka bini'matika 'alayy, wa abu'u laka bidhambi, faghfir li fa'innahu la yaghfiru al-dhunuba illa ant.' (Bukhari 6306)

**For guidance:**
'Allahumma ihdini wa saddidni' — O Allah, guide me and set me on the right course (Muslim 2725)

**For the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr):**
'Allahumma innaka 'afuwwun tuhibb al-'afwa fa'fu 'anni' — O Allah, You are the Pardoner, You love to pardon, so pardon me (Tirmidhi 3513 — sahih)

**General:**
'Rabbana atina fi al-dunya hasanatan wa fi al-akhirati hasanatan wa qina 'adhab al-nar' — Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire (Bukhari 4522 — from the Prophet's frequent du'a per Anas ibn Malik)

## Conditions of Answered Du'a

Allah promises response, but scholars distinguish three forms of response:
1. The exact du'a is granted
2. A harm equivalent to the du'a is removed
3. The reward is stored for the Hereafter

The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no Muslim who makes a du'a — containing no sin and no severing of kinship — except that Allah gives him one of three things: either He hastens its fulfilment for him in the world, or He stores it for him in the Hereafter, or He diverts an equivalent harm from him' (Ahmad — sahih per al-Arnaut).

scholar_positions: The etiquettes and times of du'a are agreed upon across all schools. The distinction between du'a directed to Allah and du'a directed to other than Allah (see Tawassul article) is the key theological division. All schools affirm that du'a to Allah is the highest form of worship; all Sunni schools agree that du'a directed to the dead is prohibited (with the detailed reasoning varying).
sources: al-Nawawi, al-Adhkar (comprehensive collection of Prophetic du'as and etiquettes)
Ibn al-Qayyim, al-Wabil al-Sayyib (on the conditions and benefits of dhikr and du'a)
Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Quran al-Azim (commentary on 2:186 and 40:60)
Said ibn Ali al-Qahtani, Hisnul Muslim (compilation of Prophetic du'as)
